AccessTokenOut.description: Shown once: ``token`` is never returned again.
AccessTokenOut.title: AccessTokenOut

display_name.description: Only you see it; defaults to external_ref.
display_name.title: Display Name

external_ref.description: Your own opaque id of the customer (no personal data).
external_ref.title: External Ref

period_anchor_day.description: The day of month (UTC) the account's periods start on, 1 to 31; in a month without that day, the month's last day. The account's monthly limits reset at the start of each period. Defaults to the UTC day of month the account is created.
period_anchor_day.title: Period Anchor Day

extra.description: Extra streaming minutes left in the current period (on an add that named the previous period: in that period).

period.description: The account's current period (unix seconds, `end` exclusive): what its monthly limits count in.

period_anchor_day.description: The day of month (UTC) the account's periods start on, 1 to 31; in a month without that day, the month's last day. The account's monthly limits reset at the start of each period.
period_anchor_day.title: Period Anchor Day

extra.description: Extra streaming minutes left in the current period (on an add that named the previous period: in that period).

period.description: The account's current period (unix seconds, `end` exclusive): what its monthly limits count in.

period_anchor_day.description: The day of month (UTC) the account's periods start on, 1 to 31; in a month without that day, the month's last day. The account's monthly limits reset at the start of each period.
period_anchor_day.title: Period Anchor Day

AccountSuspend.description:
``reason``: your own note (at most 200 characters), stored with the suspension
and never shown to anyone outside your partner.
AccountSuspend.title: AccountSuspend

AccountUpdate.description: Merge: an absent field is unchanged; ``display_name: null`` goes back to the ref.

extra.description: Set what is left of the extra streaming minutes in the current period. 409 `extra_not_applicable` while `streaming_minutes_per_month` is `"unlimited"`.

period_anchor_day.description: The day of month (UTC) the account's periods start on, 1 to 31; in a month without that day, the month's last day. The account's monthly limits reset at the start of each period. A change ends the current period at the next occurrence of the new day (its start is kept); 409 `period_change_blocked` while a session or build that started before the period current after the change (today, for a change to today's day) is still running.
period_anchor_day.title: Period Anchor Day

AccountUpdate.title: AccountUpdate

extra.description: Extra streaming minutes left in the current period (on an add that named the previous period: in that period).

period.description: The account's current period (unix seconds, `end` exclusive): what its monthly limits count in.

period_anchor_day.description: The day of month (UTC) the account's periods start on, 1 to 31; in a month without that day, the month's last day. The account's monthly limits reset at the start of each period.
period_anchor_day.title: Period Anchor Day

App.description:
An app the account can start a session on. ``access``: ``own`` (the account's own
app) or ``shared`` (an app your organization shares with your partner: the account can
list it, read it and pin a session to it, never change it); an open set. ``platform``
is an open set (`ios`, `android`, `tvos`, `androidtv` today). ``package_name``: the
app's bundle id or package name, null when not known. ``created`` is unix seconds.
App.title: App

AppLaunch.description:
Open the session's app again (with new launch parameters, for example). A session
that stays in its app (`confined` true) refuses any other app (409
`app_not_in_session`).

launch_params.description: A flat JSON object handed to the app when it is opened.
launch_params.title: Launch Params

package_name.description: The app's bundle id or package name.
package_name.title: Package Name

AppLaunch.title: AppLaunch

AppLaunchOut.description: The launch was handed to the device; it is not acknowledged by the device.
AppLaunchOut.title: AppLaunchOut

CollabCredentialCreate.description:
Turn collaboration on (a new credential) or off. ``enabled: true`` mints a
credential for one browser to watch (``view``) or also use (``control``) the session's
device; earlier credentials can still be used to connect until their ``expires_at``
unless ``regenerate`` is true, which revokes them all and disconnects
their guests. ``enabled: false`` revokes every credential and disconnects every
guest.

role.description: What the guest may do: `view` (watch) or `control` (watch and use the device: touch, keys, text, rotation, device settings, as a person's guest).
role.title: Role

ttl_seconds.description: How long a browser can connect with the credential, clamped to 3600 seconds (also the default): `expires_at` states the real one.
ttl_seconds.title: Ttl Seconds

CollabCredentialCreate.title: CollabCredentialCreate

CollabCredentialOut.description:
A collab credential for one session: give ``url`` (the guest page) or ``token`` to
ONE browser, which watches (or, with ``control``, uses) the session. A browser can
connect with this credential until ``expires_at`` (at most 3600 seconds after it is
minted). A guest that is already connected stays connected until the session ends or
you replace or disable the credential (``regenerate`` / ``enabled: false``), which
disconnects every guest. Shown once: an ``Idempotency-Key`` replay is 409
``already_created``. With collaboration turned off, ``token``, ``url``, ``expires_at``
and ``role`` are null.

expires_at.description: Unix seconds, at most 3600 seconds after the credential is minted. After `expires_at` a browser cannot connect with this credential. A guest that is already connected stays connected until the session ends or you replace or disable the credential; if its video drops after `expires_at`, the video may not come back.
expires_at.title: Expires At

token.description: The credential. Give it to one browser and keep it out of logs.
token.title: Token

url.description: The guest page for this credential.
url.title: Url

CollabCredentialOut.title: CollabCredentialOut

CollabStatusOut.description:
Whether collaboration is on for the session, how many guests are connected now,
and how many may be at once (the account's ``collab_guests_per_session``).
CollabStatusOut.title: CollabStatusOut

prices.description: Unit price per billing unit, in whole micro-USD (1,000,000 = $1.00). Keys: `streaming_minute` (per minute of streaming), `build_minute` (per metered build minute), `build_minute_over_limit` (an extra charge per build minute past an account's monthly limit, on top of `build_minute`), `storage_gb_month` (per GB-month: the daily peak storage averaged over the month, 1 GB = 10^9 bytes). Only the keys your contract sets appear; new keys may be added.
prices.title: Prices

usage_thresholds.description: Monthly usage lines across all your accounts, each list ascending. Units: `streaming_seconds`, `build_minutes`, `build_minutes_over_limit`. Only the units your contract sets appear; new units may be added.
usage_thresholds.title: Usage Thresholds

Deletion.description:
A DELETE's answer: the deletion is accepted (irreversible) and scheduled;
``account.deleted`` follows once the account is torn down.
Deletion.title: Deletion

DeviceOut.description:
A device offering a session can be started on: one per (type, category, model,
OS version), the four fields that name it. ``available``: a device of it can be
started now (VibeView's capacity as a whole, not your account's limits).

category.description: `phone`, `tablet` or `tv` (an open set). Use it exactly as returned.
category.title: Category

model.description: The device model's name, an opaque label. Use it exactly as returned.
model.title: Model

os_version.description: The OS label (the OS's name and version; its shape differs by platform), opaque. Use it exactly as returned.
os_version.title: Os Version

type.description: The platform (`ios`, `android`; an open set). Use it exactly as returned.
type.title: Type

DeviceOut.title: DeviceOut

Error.description: The error object. `code` is stable (an open set: new codes may be added); `field` names the offending member by its JSON path (`allowed_ips[0]`) when there is one; a code may add its own fields (`required_scope`, `reason`, `max`, `id`). `x-vibeview-error-codes` lists the codes known today, each with its HTTP status (null when it is sent with more than one) and its meaning.
Error.title: Error

x-vibeview-error-codes.meaning: No live access token of this account has that id.
This account is being deleted.
No account of yours has that id, or the credential cannot act in it.
A partner key names the account it acts in with `VibeView-Account`.
You suspended this account; resume it to use it.
This `Idempotency-Key` already created the object named by `id`; its secret is never shown again.
The app is not allowed to run.
The app's build cannot run on the device the session asked for.
No app this account can use has that id.
The session runs only its own app: this would open another app or leave it (Home, the app switcher, Lock).
Another request holds what this one needs; retry after `Retry-After`.
The scope's capability is not part of your contract.
The account is using as many devices at once as its limit allows.
No device of this offering is in service right now; retry later.
The session's device gave no answer in time, or could not be reached: the input may or may not have acted. Read the session before you retry, after Retry-After.
No live embed key of yours has that id.
No event of yours from the last 30 days has that id.
A live account of yours already has this `external_ref`; `account` names it.
The account's streaming_minutes_per_month is "unlimited": there are no extra minutes to give.
A request with this `Idempotency-Key` is still running; retry after `Retry-After`.
This `Idempotency-Key` was used with a different request; use a new key.
The credential lacks the scope named in `required_scope`.
An unexpected error on our side; quote `request_id` to support.
`Idempotency-Key` must be 1 to 255 visible ASCII characters, sent once.
The limit in `field` is not a whole number at or above its floor, or `unlimited` where the unit has none.
The request failed validation; `field`, when there is a member to name, names the first offending one.
The key is limited to IP ranges that do not include this request's address.
The limit in `field` is above your contract's maximum, given in `max`.

EventCutoff.description:
The cutoff a ``session.cutoff_warning`` is about: ``reason``, the end reason the
session will end with (as ``end_reason`` names it), ``ends_at``, when (unix seconds; for
the usage limit an estimate at the current rate), and ``period``, the account period the
session is measured against (a session that started in the previous period still counts
there): the ``period_start`` to name when adding extra minutes for it. A warning recorded
before late November 2026 (the feed keeps 30 days) has no ``period``.
EventCutoff.title: EventCutoff

EventData.description:
``object``, and for some event types a member beside it: ``cutoff`` on
``session.cutoff_warning``, ``reason`` on ``share.deleted`` (``requested`` or
``partner_terminated``) and on ``embed_key.revoked`` (``requested``,
``share_removed`` or ``partner_terminated``), each an open set; on ``session.created``
of a session an embed key's visitor started, ``created_via`` (``embed``), ``embed_key``
(the key's id) and ``visitor`` (the visitor token's ``sub``); each absent from every
other event.
EventData.title: EventData

EventOut.description:
An event as its webhook delivered it (``id``, ``type``, ``created``,
``api_version``, ``partner``, ``account``, ``data``), plus ``object`` and
``livemode``. Kept 30 days. A field the envelope gains later is passed through. Every event type is listed in `x-vibeview-event-types`; a type with `sent: false` is not sent yet. New types may be added.
EventOut.title: EventOut

Extra.description:
Extra streaming minutes of the account: used only after the period's monthly
minutes are used up, and ending with the period (`expires_at`, unix seconds, the period's
`end`): what is left is not carried over.

streaming_minutes.description: What is left now, in whole minutes rounded down.
streaming_minutes.title: Streaming Minutes

Extra.title: Extra

ExtraMinutesAdd.description: Extra streaming minutes to add to one period of the account.

period_start.description: The period to add to, by its start (unix seconds, as `period.start` and `cutoff.period.start` give it). Default: the account's current period. The previous period is accepted only while a session that started in it is still running (to extend that session); any other value is 422 `invalid_request`.
period_start.title: Period Start

streaming_minutes.description: Minutes to add, 1 to 100,000. A period's added total is at most 1,000,000 (422 `invalid_request`).
streaming_minutes.title: Streaming Minutes

ExtraMinutesAdd.title: ExtraMinutesAdd

ExtraUpdate.description: Set what is left of the account's extra streaming minutes in its current period.

streaming_minutes.description: What is LEFT of the account's extra streaming minutes in its current period from now on, 0 to 100,000, in whole minutes (up to 59 seconds can remain). It replaces whatever was added before it, including an add a moment earlier: use `POST .../extra-minutes` while sessions run, and this to settle. It is the account's whole period, not one session's: with other sessions running, leave what they still need (0 only when none is running).
streaming_minutes.title: Streaming Minutes

ExtraUpdate.title: ExtraUpdate

build_minutes_per_month.description: Cloud build minutes per period of the account.
build_minutes_per_month.title: Build Minutes Per Month

streaming_minutes_per_month.description: Streaming minutes per period of the account.
streaming_minutes_per_month.title: Streaming Minutes Per Month

PartnerEmbedKey.description:
An embed key of your partner on an app your organization shares with it. ``id`` is
the key itself: public by design (it sits in the embedding page). Every session it
starts needs a visitor token signed with its visitor secret. ``platform`` is an open
set. Never the visitor secret.
PartnerEmbedKey.title: PartnerEmbedKey

PartnerOut.description:
The partner a credential belongs to, its environment and, for an access token,
its account.

account.description: The access token's account (`org_...`); `null` for a partner key, which acts in no one account.
account.title: Account

id.description: The partner's id (`ptn_...`), for the paths under `/api/v1/partners/{ptn}/`.
id.title: Id

livemode.description: `true` for a live partner, `false` for a test partner.
livemode.title: Livemode

name.description: The partner's name, as VibeView set it up with you.
name.title: Name

PartnerOut.title: PartnerOut

since.description: Unix seconds; at most 30 days back, never before the endpoint existed.
since.title: Since

SessionControl.description:
One input to the device, as a person's live input. Coordinates are in the
device's screen pixels as the session's screenshots show them. On a session that stays
in its app (`confined` true), a button or key that leaves the app (HOME, APP_SWITCH,
RECENTS, LOCK, SIDE_BUTTON, SIRI, APPLE_PAY) is refused (409 `app_not_in_session`).

action.description: The input: tap, swipe, rotate, shake, button, key, touch_*.
action.title: Action

keycode.description: Android: BACK, MENU, DPAD_UP and so on.
keycode.title: Keycode

SessionControl.title: SessionControl

SessionControlOut.description:
The input was handed to the device. It is not acknowledged by the device: read the
screen (the agent tools) to see its effect.
SessionControlOut.title: SessionControlOut

SessionCreate.description:
A new session in the account. Name the device offering with the four fields
exactly as `GET /devices/pools` lists it, and the app the account can use (`GET
/apps`: its own, or one shared with your partner) to install and open, with launch
parameters for it. A session needs an app: without one the request is refused (422
`invalid_request`, `field` `app`). The session installs the app's newest build, or the
one `build` names. The session stays in its app: other apps, Home and the app switcher
are not available on its device, unless `confined` is `false` and your contract
includes sessions that can leave their app. `labels` tag the session; with `reuse` the
account's live session with the same labels, app, `build`, `confined` and offering is
returned instead of a new one. Any other member is refused.

app.description: An app the account can use, by its id as `GET /apps` lists it (its own, or one shared with your partner), to install and open. Required: a request without it is refused (422 `invalid_request`).
app.title: App

build.description: One build of `app` to install, by its build id (the build's `public_id`, as the organization that uploaded it reads it in its own list of the app's builds). Without it the session installs the app's newest build. A build that is not one of the app's, whose file has expired, or that cannot run on the device offering is refused (422 `invalid_request`, `field` `build`).
build.title: Build

confined.description: `true` (the default): the session stays in its app. `false`: a session that can leave its app (Home, the app switcher and other apps work, as on a person's device), only when your contract includes it; otherwise 403 `unconfined_sessions_not_allowed`. `app` is required either way.
confined.title: Confined

device_category.description: `phone`, `tablet` or `tv` (an open set). Use it exactly as returned.
device_category.title: Device Category

device_type.description: The device's platform: `ios` or `android`, as `GET /devices/pools` lists it.
device_type.title: Device Type

labels.description: Up to 10 labels of your own for the session, returned on it and in its events. Keys and values are 1 to 64 characters of letters, digits and `. _ : -`; a key given twice keeps its last value. Not for personal data.
labels.title: Labels

launch_params.description: A flat JSON object handed to the app when it is opened (only with `app`). Not applied when `reuse` returns a session that already exists.
launch_params.title: Launch Params

model.description: The device model's name, an opaque label. Use it exactly as returned.
model.title: Model

os_version.description: The OS label (the OS's name and version; its shape differs by platform), opaque. Use it exactly as returned.
os_version.title: Os Version

reuse.description: Return the account's live session (pending, starting or active) that was created through this route with exactly the same `labels`, `app`, `build`, `confined` and device offering, instead of creating another (answered 200 with `reused: true`). Needs at least one label.
reuse.title: Reuse

SessionCreate.title: SessionCreate

SessionCreated.description:
The session `POST /sessions/` created (201, `reused` false), or the live session
that `reuse` found (200, `reused` true).

build.description: The pinned build's id (the `build` the session was created with); null when the session follows the app's newest build, or when the pinned build has since been deleted.
build.title: Build

confined.description: `true`: the session stays in its app (Home, the app switcher and other apps are not available). `false`: it was created with `confined: false` and can leave its app.
confined.title: Confined

labels.description: The labels the session was created with (an empty object for none).
labels.title: Labels

reused.description: True when `reuse` returned a session that already existed.
reused.title: Reused

streaming_seconds.description: The session's metered streaming time so far, in whole seconds rounded down: what the account's usage counts for it (up to now while it runs; 0 until it reached a device, and 0 while it is stopping, as the usage record counts it then). The sessions of a day can sum to up to one second per session less than that day's usage record.
streaming_seconds.title: Streaming Seconds

SessionCreated.title: SessionCreated

SessionDevice.description:
What a session runs on, as an offering (never an instance): the four fields
of a ``DeviceOut``. A session waiting for any phone or tablet has no category or
model yet (null).

category.description: `phone`, `tablet` or `tv` (an open set). Use it exactly as returned.
category.title: Category

model.description: The device model's name, an opaque label. Use it exactly as returned.
model.title: Model

os_version.description: The OS label (the OS's name and version; its shape differs by platform), opaque. Use it exactly as returned.
os_version.title: Os Version

type.description: The platform (`ios`, `android`; an open set). Use it exactly as returned.
type.title: Type

SessionDevice.title: SessionDevice

SessionOut.description:
A session of the account. ``status`` and ``end_reason`` are open sets (new
values may appear): ``status`` is one of pending, starting, active, stopping,
stopped, failed today. ``created``, ``started``, ``ended`` are unix seconds.

build.description: The pinned build's id (the `build` the session was created with); null when the session follows the app's newest build, or when the pinned build has since been deleted.
build.title: Build

confined.description: `true`: the session stays in its app (Home, the app switcher and other apps are not available). `false`: it was created with `confined: false` and can leave its app.
confined.title: Confined

labels.description: The labels the session was created with (an empty object for none).
labels.title: Labels

streaming_seconds.description: The session's metered streaming time so far, in whole seconds rounded down: what the account's usage counts for it (up to now while it runs; 0 until it reached a device, and 0 while it is stopping, as the usage record counts it then). The sessions of a day can sum to up to one second per session less than that day's usage record.
streaming_seconds.title: Streaming Seconds

SessionOut.title: SessionOut

SessionPresenceOut.description:
The session is held by your credential until ``expires_at`` (unix seconds): call
again before it. ``idle_ends_at`` (unix seconds, null while the session is not
active): if no input or driving tool call arrives before it, the session ends for
inactivity, not before this time (then, or up to a minute and a half later).
SessionPresenceOut.title: SessionPresenceOut

SessionQueueOut.description:
A session waiting for a device: its 1-based ``position`` among the waiters for
the same offering, and why it waits (``reason``, an open set, null when unknown:
``account_limit`` the account's concurrent sessions are in use, ``partner_limit``
your accounts together use every session you may run at once, ``devices_busy``
every matching device is in use, ``devices_updating`` the matching devices are
being updated or a free one is being prepared).
SessionQueueOut.title: SessionQueueOut

SessionWarning.description:
Something about the session to act on: ``code`` (an open set: new codes may
appear) and a fixed sentence for it.
SessionWarning.title: SessionWarning

ShareOut.description:
Something your organization shares with your partner. ``kind``: ``app`` (an open
set). ``app`` (the app's id), ``app_name`` and ``platform`` (an open set) are null for
a share that is not an app.
ShareOut.title: ShareOut

ToolCall.description: One agent tool call: the tool's name and its arguments.

tool.description: One of the tools listed in the operation.
tool.title: Tool

ToolCall.title: ToolCall

ToolIdleWarning.description: The session is close to its inactivity end (set only on reading tools).
ToolIdleWarning.title: ToolIdleWarning

ToolObservation.description:
What the screen showed after the tool ran: ``kind`` ``full`` (the whole tree),
``diff`` (what changed), ``unchanged`` or ``unavailable`` (it could not be read).
ToolObservation.title: ToolObservation

ToolResultOut.description:
A tool call that reached the device, as the tool layer answers it.

``ok`` is false when the tool refused (``result.status`` ``error``, the reason in
``result.message``), ran but missed (``result.status`` ``warning``, the reason in
``result.warning``: a tap, long press, drag or alert that did not land, a
``scroll_until_visible`` that never found its text), or typed into a field that does
not hold the text afterwards (``type_text`` / ``clear_text``: ``result.verified``
false, with a ``warning``; ``verified`` null means it could not be checked and is
still ``ok``). ``find_element`` finding nothing is ``ok`` true with
``result.found`` false and a ``message``. ``logs`` is ``ok`` false with a
``message`` when the app's log is not available.

``result`` is the tool's own answer: for ``screenshot`` a string, an inline data URL
(``data:image/png;base64,...``), or with ``args.preview: true`` an object
``{image, preview: {data_url, mime_type, width, height, bytes}}``; null for
``ui_tree``; an object for every other tool. ``observation`` is the screen after the
tool (``kind`` ``full``, ``diff``, ``unchanged`` or ``unavailable``, and ``text``),
null for ``screenshot`` and ``logs``. ``idle_warning`` is null unless a reading tool
ran close to the inactivity end. A device that gave no answer is never a result: it is
503 ``device_unreachable``.

``reason`` (null unless ``ok`` is false because the device refused the tool's action),
an open set (new values may appear: handle one you do not know as ``action_failed``):
``element_not_visible`` (the element is not visible or is covered), ``gesture_failed``
(a scroll, drag or long press could not be completed), ``alert_failed`` (no alert could
be answered), ``no_app_launched`` (no app is in the foreground), ``link_not_opened``
(the app did not open the link), ``app_not_in_session`` (the session stays in its app:
the tool would open another app or leave it, such as ``press_button`` home, or a link on
iOS), ``action_failed`` (any other refusal). Its sentence is in the result's
text.
ToolResultOut.title: ToolResultOut

Usage.description:
The account's current period so far (``period``: unix seconds, ``end``
exclusive). Whole numbers only: ``streaming_seconds`` (sessions that started in the
period, live ones included, rounded down), ``build_minutes`` (every metered minute of
the period's finished builds, within the limit or past it, each build rounded up to
whole minutes as it is metered), ``storage_bytes`` (stored now).
Usage.title: Usage

UsageCurrentPeriod.description: The account's current period so far, computed at `as_of` (unix seconds).
UsageCurrentPeriod.title: UsageCurrentPeriod

UsageList.description:
A page of usage records, ordered by day, account, unit. `current_period` is set
when the page is one account's and `to` is today or later; null otherwise.
UsageList.title: UsageList

UsagePrice.description:
The unit price of the contract in force at the end of the record's day, for the
unit's price key (`streaming_minute`, `build_minute`, `build_minute_over_limit`,
`storage_gb_month`), in whole micro-dollars (1,000,000 = $1.00). Never an amount: a
month's amount is computed from the month's records and their prices.

sent change), ``period_anchor_day`` (a change cuts the current period; 409

post.description:
Give the account extra streaming minutes for one period: used only once the period's
monthly minutes are used up, and ending with it. Additive: each call adds
``streaming_minutes`` (1 to 100,000; a period's total at most 1,000,000), so send an
``Idempotency-Key`` (a repeat returns the first answer and adds nothing). ``period_start``
(unix seconds) defaults to the current period; the previous period's start is accepted
while a session that started in it still runs (``session.cutoff_warning`` names it).
Answers the account, its ``extra`` being what is left in that period. 409
``extra_not_applicable`` when ``streaming_minutes_per_month`` is ``"unlimited"``.

post.description: Creates a pending session in the account on a device offering: the four fields exactly as `GET /devices/pools` lists them. Names the app the account can use (`GET /apps`) to install and open: a session needs one (without it, 422 `invalid_request` with `field` `app`), and it stays in that app unless `confined` is `false` (only when your contract includes sessions that can leave their app; otherwise 403 `unconfined_sessions_not_allowed`); an id it cannot use is 404 `app_not_found`. Start it with `POST /sessions/{session_id}/start`. An offering that exists but has no device in service right now is 409 `device_unavailable` (retry later); anything else that is not an offering is 422 `invalid_request` naming the field. Refused with 403 `concurrent_sessions_limit` when the account uses all the devices it may use at once, `partner_concurrent_sessions_limit` when your accounts together do, and `streaming_minutes_exhausted` when the account has no streaming minutes left. With `labels` and `reuse: true`, a live session of the account created here with exactly the same labels, app, `build`, `confined` and offering is returned instead (200, `reused: true`), never refused at a limit; its `launch_params` are not applied again. While another request with the same labels is creating one, 409 `session_create_in_progress` (retry in a moment).

post.description:
Reads or drives the device of an active session, one tool per call. The tools:

- `ui_tree`: the screen's elements as text, each interactive one with a ref (`@e1`) the other tools take.
- `screenshot`: the screen as an inline PNG data URL (`args.preview: true` adds a smaller copy).
- `logs`: the app's recent log lines (`args.since`, `args.tail`).
- `find_element`: find an element by its text or id.
- `wait`: wait up to 30 seconds (`args.seconds`).
- `tap`: tap an element by ref.
- `tap_coordinates`: tap at screen coordinates.
- `long_press`: press and hold an element or a point.
- `swipe`: swipe in a direction or between two points.
- `scroll_until_visible`: scroll until a text or id is on screen.
- `gesture_preset`: one of a fixed set of gestures.
- `drag`: drag from one point to another.
- `alert`: answer a system alert with one of its buttons.
- `type_text`: type text into the focused field.
- `clear_text`: clear the focused field.
- `press_button`: press a device button (back, the TV remote's keys; on a session that stays in its app, home, recents, lock and siri leave the app and are refused: `reason` `app_not_in_session`).
- `open_url`: open a link: on a session that stays in its app, Android sends it as a view intent to the session's app only and iOS opens no link (`reason` `app_not_in_session`); on a session that can leave its app, iOS opens the link as given (a web link in the browser) and Android sends it to the app the session last opened, normally the session's app (it opens there or the tool fails).
- `set_posture`: fold or unfold a foldable device.
- `rotate`: rotate the device.
- `shake`: shake the device.
- `set_location`: set the device's simulated location.
- `set_status_bar`: show a clean status bar or the device's real one.
- `set_app_language`: run the app in another language (the app restarts).
- `relaunch_app`: close the app and start it again.
- `tap_focused_tv`: select the focused element (TV).
- `focus_element_tv`: move the focus to an element (TV).

The reading tools (`ui_tree`, `screenshot`, `logs`, `find_element`, `wait`) keep the session held but are not use; every other tool is use. A `screenshot` result is an inline data URL (`data:image/png;base64,...`), never a link. A tool that reached the device answers 200 with `ok` (see the result object for what `ok` false means and where its reason is). A tool outside this list is 422 `tool_refused`; bad `args` 422 `invalid_request` (`type_text` at most 10000 characters, `scroll_until_visible` at most 50 scrolls, `wait` at most 30 seconds; the body at most 64 KB). A session that is not `active` is 409 `session_not_active`, an ended one 409 `session_ended`, one whose app is not in front yet (or is being brought back) 409 `session_not_ready` (every tool, reads included; retry in a few seconds), a device that cannot run agent tools 409 `tool_refused`. A device that gave no answer (it did not reply in time, or nothing reached it) is 503 `device_unreachable` with `Retry-After`: the tool may or may not have acted. One tool runs on a session at a time; when 4 more already wait, a call is 429 `rate_limited` (`limit` `session_tools`, `Retry-After`). Not idempotent (no `Idempotency-Key`: a repeated tap is a second tap); read the session before retrying.

put.description: Mints a collab credential for one session of the account. Hand `url` (the guest page) or `token` to the browser that should watch (`role` `view`) or also use the device (`control`: touch, keys, text, rotation and device settings, as a person's guest; no command to open a URL or deep link is accepted from a guest): never your key or access token, which must not reach a browser. A browser can connect with it until `expires_at` (at most 3600 seconds after it is minted; `ttl_seconds` is clamped). A guest that is already connected stays connected until the session ends or you replace or disable the credential (`regenerate` / `enabled: false`), which disconnects every guest. Calling it again mints another credential: earlier ones can still be used to connect until their `expires_at`, unless `regenerate` is true, which revokes them and disconnects their guests; `enabled: false` revokes every credential and disconnects every guest. Guests count against the account's `collab_guests_per_session`: a guest over it is refused. A connected guest keeps the session held (no presence calls are needed while one watches); watching is not use, a `control` guest's input is, so a session nobody uses still ends `inactivity_timeout`. An ended session is 409 `session_ended`. The answer is shown once (`Cache-Control: no-store`): a repeat with the same `Idempotency-Key` is 409 `already_created` naming the session; a repeat of `enabled: false` returns its answer again.

post.description: Sends one input (a tap, a swipe, a button or key press, a rotation, a shake, a touch) to the device of an active session, as a person's live input. Any other `action` is 422 `invalid_request`. On a session that stays in its app (`confined` true), a button or key that would leave it (Home, the app switcher, Lock, Siri) is 409 `app_not_in_session` and is not sent. Not idempotent (no `Idempotency-Key`: a repeated input is a second input); read the session before retrying. A session that is not `active` is 409 `session_not_active`, an ended one 409 `session_ended`, one whose app is not in front yet (or is being brought back) 409 `session_not_ready` (retry in a few seconds); a device that cannot be reached is 503 `device_unreachable` (retry after `Retry-After`).

post.description: A session driven from your server has no viewer: call this while you use it. Each call holds the session for 60 seconds (`expires_at`); call it every 15 seconds. An active session that nobody holds ends `no_client` about two minutes after it became active, or soon after the hold lapses. Holding is not use: a session with no input for the account's idle timeout still ends `inactivity_timeout`, not before `idle_ends_at` (send input or a driving tool call before it; null until the session is active). A pending or starting session may be held; a waiting session's 30 minutes are not extended by it. A stopping session is 409 `session_not_active`, an ended one 409 `session_ended`.

post.description: Starts a pending session on a device of its offering. When none is free the session waits: it stays `pending` with `queue` set and starts when a device frees. A waiting session that gets no device within 30 minutes of this call ends: `failed`, with `end_reason` `queue_timeout` (a `session.ended` event is sent). A session already starting, active or waiting is returned as it is; an ended one is 409 `session_ended`. The waiting sessions of one account are capped at the number of devices it may use at once (429 `queue_full`, with `Retry-After`).
